title: Nocturne in E-flat Major
technique: Let the melody sing above the accompaniment, keep the broken chords soft and even, and shape long phrases.
body: Nocturne in E-flat Major is a complete piano song in E-flat major, in 4/4 at 76 beats per minute, built as an original realization of a public-domain nocturne framework. A nocturne framework is a night piece, with a long singing melody floating over gently broken chords, quiet and expressive. The form runs Opening, Middle, Return, Closing across 32 bars, with 256 notes for both hands and a total playing time of 101.1 seconds. To play it, let the melody sing above the accompaniment, keep the broken chords soft and even, and shape long phrases. The framework itself belongs to the public musical language, while this melodic realization is original and is not attributed to any composer.

The framework itself belongs to the public musical language, while this melodic realization is original and is not attributed to any composer.

title: Etude-Style Study in C Minor
technique: Practice the pattern evenly first, then play it as music, keeping the pattern clean at full speed.
body: Etude-Style Study in C Minor is a complete piano song in C minor, in 4/4 at 120 beats per minute, built as an original realization of a public-domain etude framework. An etude-style framework is a study built around one technical pattern, repeated and developed until the pattern itself becomes the music. The form runs Study A, Study B, Study Return, Closing across 32 bars, with 384 notes for both hands and a total playing time of 64.0 seconds. To play it, practice the pattern evenly first, then play it as music, keeping the pattern clean at full speed. The framework itself belongs to the public musical language, while this melodic realization is original and is not attributed to any composer.

title: Etude-Style Study in A Minor
technique: Practice the pattern evenly first, then play it as music, keeping the pattern clean at full speed.
body: Etude-Style Study in A Minor is a complete piano song in A minor, in 4/4 at 124 beats per minute, built as an original realization of a public-domain etude framework. An etude-style framework is a study built around one technical pattern, repeated and developed until the pattern itself becomes the music. The form runs Study A, Study B, Study Return, Closing across 32 bars, with 384 notes for both hands and a total playing time of 61.9 seconds. To play it, practice the pattern evenly first, then play it as music, keeping the pattern clean at full speed. The framework itself belongs to the public musical language, while this melodic realization is original and is not attributed to any composer.

body: Waltz in D-flat Major is a complete piano song in D-flat major, in 3/4 at 132 beats per minute, built as an original realization of a public-domain waltz framework. A waltz framework is a dance in triple time, with a bass note on the first beat and light chords on the second and third beats under a flowing melody. The form runs First Waltz, Second Waltz, Return, Coda across 32 bars, with 320 notes for both hands and a total playing time of 43.6 seconds. To play it, stress the first beat gently, keep the chords light, and let the melody flow over the dance pulse. The framework itself belongs to the public musical language, while this melodic realization is original and is not attributed to any composer.
